clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. E s t a b lis h m e n t  o f  th e  B o a r d . There is established effective July 10,  
1982, a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate  
this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise  
interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. R e p o r t. The board shall report its finding to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days from the date of its creation.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. M a in t a in in g  C o n d it io n s . A s provided by Section 10 of the Railway  
Labor Act, as amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board  
and for 30 days after the board has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be made by the carriers or by their  
employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12370 (47 FR 30047, Federal Register of July 12, 1982; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Certain Railroads Represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference and signed July 8, 1982. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and certain railroads represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 3 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (sec1; sec2; sec3). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; they are not recorded as later events because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence, so the claim states the functional spending without a date. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in an emergency-board report held under jobs/source-ladder. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
